label: Terrain dock minimized
verdict:
**Not perfect — a handful of minor issues, no layout-breaking overlaps in the main stage:**

- **Sidebar last item clipped — [minor]** — The "Patio" row under *Patios & Paths* (left sidebar, ~y750–780) is cut off mid-item by the bottom status bar. If the list scrolls that's forgivable, but there's no scroll cue/fade, so it reads as broken. Fix: bottom padding or partial-item fade.
- **Duplicate active "Terrain" controls — [minor]** — "Terrain" is highlighted in both the floating SCULPT panel (~300, 450) and as an active bottom pill (~800, 707), sitting next to "Sculpt ▸". A new user can't tell which of the three is actually the tool switch. Consolidate or de-dupe.
- **Redundant "Analyze" — [minor]** — Appears three times: in the SCULPT group (~310, 530), as a bottom pill (~1000, 707), and as the bottom-right floating chart button. Clutter suggests a design slip.
- **"Innovate" label — [minor/content]** — Bottom-right pill likely should be "Irrigate" in a yard-design context; "Innovate" reads like a typo and is meaningless as a tool action.
- **"FPS: —" — [nit]** — Permanent dash placeholder in the status bar looks like an unhandled empty state; hide it until FPS is reported.

No overlapping or clipped elements found in the toolbar, viewport overlays (Tape Measure / Terrain / Excavate pills, Terrain Sculpting panel, scale bar, Sun button), compass, or zoom controls — they're all cleanly separated. With the "Getting Started" tip and named 3D view, a new user would grasp the screen within a few seconds; the duplicated Terrain/Analyze controls are the main 5-second-test friction point.
